questions.q: What are a Delta table's actual data files, underneath?
options: Ordinary Parquet files, unchanged — Delta wraps Parquet rather than replacing it
A completely proprietary binary format unrelated to Parquet
Plain CSV files with an added header
JSON files stored in a special Delta-only encoding
questions.explain: This connects directly to Foundations Lesson 42's explanation of why Parquet is the default analytics format.

questions.q: What problem does plain Parquet have that Delta Lake solves?
options: Writing a batch of Parquet files isn't atomic — a failed or interrupted write can leave a partial, inconsistent set of files with no way to detect it
Parquet files cannot be read by Spark at all
Parquet files take up more disk space than any other format
Parquet doesn't support columnar storage
questions.explain: Two concurrent writers can also create conflicting output with nothing to detect or prevent it.

options: A sequential, append-only log of every change ever made to the table — which files were added, removed, and when
A backup copy of the table's data, in case of accidental deletion
A folder containing only error messages from failed writes
A configuration file listing the table's column names
questions.explain: This log is the actual mechanism behind atomic writes, time travel, and safe concurrent UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE.

questions.q: Why do real Databricks pipelines default to Delta tables over plain Parquet?
options: Delta tables are still Parquet underneath, but add real correctness guarantees for a genuinely small extra cost
Plain Parquet cannot be read by Spark, only by Delta-aware tools
Delta Lake is required by Azure Databricks and Parquet cannot be used at all
There's no real reason; it's purely a stylistic convention
questions.explain: Plain Parquet is now the exception, reserved for cases with a specific reason not to use Delta.

questions.q: Why didn't Foundations' PySpark material need to worry about the atomicity problem Delta Lake solves?
options: Every read/write in that course ran once, start to finish, uninterrupted — the partial-write scenario never came up
Foundations already used Delta Lake throughout, without naming it
PySpark automatically guarantees atomicity for every write regardless of format
Foundations never wrote any data to disk at all
questions.explain: This is exactly the gap Delta Lake's transaction log closes for real, unattended, concurrent production pipelines.
